subject: Climate & Environment
title: Boreal Forests of the North
description: A short lesson to help you apply Boreal Forests of the North.

hook.text: The boreal forest wraps around the top of the world — the largest land biome on Earth.

buildup.text: It stretches across Canada, Russia, and Scandinavia — 17 million square kilometers.

discovery.text: Boreal forests store twice as much carbon as tropical forests, mostly in their soil.

twist.text: Climate change is warming the Arctic faster, drying out boreal forests and fueling wildfires.

climax.text: Canada's boreal now burns so much each year that it has flipped from carbon sink to source.

punchline.text: The quiet forests of the north hold more carbon — and more risk.

quiz.question: Where do boreal forests store most of their carbon?

details.summary: Boreal forests form a vast band of spruce, pine, and larch across Canada, Russia, and Scandinavia, storing roughly one-third of all terrestrial carbon, mostly in soils. They are increasingly threatened by logging, mining, wildfire, and insect outbreaks intensified by warming.
details.whyItMatters: Boreal forests contain more carbon than tropical forests, yet receive far less conservation attention. Their loss or degradation through fire and thaw releases ancient stored carbon.
takeaways: Boreal forests cover roughly 17 million square kilometers globally
Their soils store more carbon than their trees do
Wildfires in boreal regions are increasing in frequency and intensity

faq.question: Why do boreal soils store so much carbon?
faq.answer: Cold temperatures slow decomposition, causing dead plant material to accumulate in thick organic layers over thousands of years. Some boreal soils sit atop permafrost, which further locks in carbon until warming triggers thaw.

faq.question: How is climate change affecting boreal forests?
faq.answer: Warming is lengthening fire seasons, expanding bark beetle outbreaks, thawing permafrost beneath roots, and shifting tree lines northward. Some areas are transitioning from carbon sinks to carbon sources as disturbance outpaces regrowth.
